sources.citation: Roberts, James. 2025. The vowel system of Ndam. Afrika und Übersee 98: 63-80. DOI 10.15460/auue.2025.98.1.387 (CC BY 4.0).
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing. Whole article read: surface consonant/vowel inventories (sec. 2), morphophonemic alternations, prosodies of palatalization and labialization; 'stress', 'accent', 'pitch' = 0 hits, 'tone' only in a cited title (Jungraithmayr 1977), no tone or stress marks on any data. It names the other Ndam descriptions: Broß 1988, Cray 2006 grammar sketch (ms.), Cray 2012a lexicon (ms.), Cray 2012b verb inflections (ms.).

sources.citation: Roberts, James. 2021. Initial findings on the Boor language. Afrika und Übersee 94 (Chadic colloquium section). DOI 10.15460/auue.2021.94.1.242.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: About Boor, not Ndam; Ndam appears only as comparative wordlist items (numerals etc., from Cray 2012 and Broß 1988) and a 25% lexical-similarity figure. No stress or tone statement for Ndam (the only tone remark concerns Boor: tone markings impressionistic, not presented).

sources.citation: Glottolog 5.3 reference list for ndam1251 (12 refs) and for sister languages Somrai somr1248 (26) and Tumak tuma1260 (14).
sources.note: Besides Broß 1988 and Roberts 2025, the Ndam list holds only wordlists/travel reports (Benton 1912, Gaudefroy-Demombynes 1907, Chevalier 1907, Decorse 1906, Bruel 1905, Vossart 1971), Jungraithmayr & Ibriszimow 1994 Chadic Lexical Roots, Sommer 1992, Ethnologue. No phonology or grammar of Ndam other than Broß.

sources.citation: Jungraithmayr, Herrmann & Carsten Peust. 2021. A Sketch of Sarwa, a Chadic Minority Language in Central Chad. ZDMG 171(1).
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.access_detail: publisher DOI, paywalled; library e-access not checked
sources.note: The item the earlier scan cited as 'Ndam material pp. 32-36'; it is a Sarwa sketch, but Jungraithmayr collected Ndam-Dik data in the 1970s and the sketch may include comparative Ndam forms with tone marking. Low priority: not a Ndam description.

sources.citation: Cray, William. 2006. A grammar sketch of Ndam. N'Djaména: AIM (Africa Inland Mission). Ms.
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.note: Unpublished missionary grammar sketch cited by Roberts 2025; a sketch normally opens with a phonology section that would note tone/stress. Obtainable only through SIL Chad / AIM (James Roberts, SIL Chad, is the contact).

sources.citation: Broß, Michael. 1988. Materialien zur Sprache der Ndam von Dik (Republik Tschad): Untersuchungen zur Phonologie und Morphologie. MA thesis, Philipps-Universität Marburg, 118 pp.
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.access_detail: print only (no digital copy found when the work was looked up)
sources.note: The only description of Ndam with a phonology chapter (Glottolog's sole descriptive ref; Roberts 2025 calls it the one existing monograph). Its suprasegmental section is the one place a stress/tone statement for Ndam can be expected.
